hero.eyebrow: Al Haram · Giza · the twelfth floor
hero.title: Three pyramids, {km} km from your pillow
hero.lead: A guest house on the top floor of an ordinary Giza apartment block, which is the whole point: at this height you stand level with the base of the Great Pyramid, and the rooftops of Al Haram fall away below Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure.
hero.sub: Cairo never stops honking. Take the lift to the twelfth floor and the street drops away: Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure fill the window, and breakfast is on the roof.
hero.badgeBottom: level with the Great Pyramid’s base

facts.view: Level with the Great Pyramid's base

rooms.intro: Twelve rooms on the twelfth floor, in five kinds. Every one has air conditioning, its own bathroom and free Wi‑Fi, and breakfast on the roof is included. The twin rooms on the west side have the pyramids in the window.
rooms.stay: By the night, for a few days or a longer stay: ask us
rooms.bathroomText: Breakfast is served on the open roof terrace from seven to nine, with the plateau laid out in front of you; in the evening it is where guests sit for the sound-and-light show. Tea and coffee all day.

twin-view.name: Twin room, pyramids view
twin-view.short: Two large beds, the pyramids in the window
twin-view.desc: Two large beds with velvet headboards and a picture window that frames all three pyramids. A table by the glass with a kettle tray, a minibar, a dressing table. Room 5 is one of these: from the door, the Great Pyramid fills the window.

studio.name: Deluxe studio
studio.short: A queen bed, a kitchenette and a sitting corner
studio.desc: The largest and newest room on the floor: a queen bed against a wood-panelled wall, a black-marble kitchenette, a velvet armchair, a table for two in the sun, and a bathroom with a glass shower. For a longer stay, or a couple who wants space.

triple.name: Triple room
triple.short: A double and a single bed
triple.desc: A double bed and a single side by side under a wide window over Giza, in warm beige. For a family of three or three friends.

twin.name: Twin room
twin.desc: Two single beds with sage-green covers, a wardrobe, a small fridge, a curved mirror and a bathroom with a glass shower. For friends or colleagues travelling together.

double.name: Double room
double.desc: A double bed with a velvet headboard, a window over the rooftops, a dressing shelf and an oval mirror, and its own bathroom. The simplest room, a few steps from the roof where the view is. Room 8 is one of these.

view.title: What you see from the balcony
view.text: The guest house faces due west across the rooftops of Al Haram to the plateau. From left to right: Menkaure, the smallest; Khafre, which looks tallest because it stands on higher ground and still wears its casing at the top; and Khufu, the Great Pyramid. At sunset the sun drops between them.

giza.intro: The house is in Al Haram, the district that grew up along Pyramids Road, a long straight avenue from the Nile to the plateau. West is the site; north is the new museum; east, past the metro, is Cairo proper. South along the river are the older pyramids, Saqqara and Dahshur, where the builders practised.
giza.byAir: From Cairo Airport: about an hour by car across the city; the house arranges pickup. From Sphinx Airport: 40 minutes on the desert road.
giza.byMetro: Metro Line 2 to El Monib, then a short taxi ride down Al Haram road.
giza.byRoad: By car: Al Haram (Pyramids) Road from the Nile, turn south at Abd Al Aziz Al Basel Street.

elev.title: Profile from the house to the plateau
elev.roofs: rooftops of Al Haram, about {m} m
elev.note: Heights are approximate; the vertical scale is stretched 2.5 times.
elev.caption: The twelfth floor stands at roughly {floor} m above the sea, the base of the Great Pyramid at {base}: the whole pyramid rises above the rooftops in front of you.
elev.text: Al Haram is flat and low. The plateau to the west rises about forty metres above it, and the pyramids stand on top of that rise. From a ground-floor window you would see apartment blocks. From the twelfth floor the line of sight clears the roofs, and all three pyramids stand against the sky, base to apex.

day.title: A day on the twelfth floor
day.hint: Drag the sun round the ring, or tap a moment.

dawn.d: The sun comes up behind you, over Cairo, and lights the pyramids from the east. The clearest view of the day is in the first hour.

breakfast.d: Seven to nine on the open terrace: ful, falafel, eggs, bread, white cheese, fruit, tea. The plateau is laid out in front of your table.

checkout.d: Check-out is at eleven; the Sphinx entrance is a short ride down the road. Go early, before the coaches and the heat.

checkin.d: Rooms are ready from two. Midday haze flattens the view; it is a good hour for the air conditioning and a sleep.

afternoon.d: By four the light turns and the pyramids come back out of the haze. The balcony faces them squarely.

sunset.d: The sun drops behind the plateau. Depending on the month it sets to the left of Menkaure or between Khafre and Khufu; in late October it is on the left.

dusk.d: Twenty minutes of pink and violet, the pyramids as cut-outs, the lights of Al Haram coming on below.

show.d: The plateau is lit in colour from the Sphinx side. You watch it from the terrace, with the commentary carrying up on still nights.

night.d: The pyramids go dark; the city does not. The lift runs all night and someone is at the desk.

practical.intro: What the listings say, in one place.
items: Air conditioning, a private bathroom and a fridge in every room; Wi‑Fi throughout; a lift to the twelfth floor.
Check-in from 14:00, check-out by 11:00, breakfast 07:00 to 09:00. Someone is at the desk all night.
Airport pickup for a fee: give us your flight. Metro Line 2 to El Monib, then a taxi down Pyramids Road.
Cars and guides to Saqqara, Dahshur, Memphis and the museums, booked at the desk.
English, Arabic, French, German, Dutch, Portuguese, Russian.

ride.title: Cairo is loud. The lift takes forty seconds.

g.p: Al Haram at full volume. Microbuses stopping wherever a hand goes up, horns in three keys, tea glasses on a tin tray, a man who would like to sell you a camel ride. This is the Cairo of twenty million people, and it is a good part of why you came.

f4.t: The horns turn into a hum
f4.p: Four floors up the street is already a sound, not a place. Laundry on the lines, and every satellite dish on every balcony looking at the same patch of sky.

f8.p: Water tanks, pigeon lofts on stilts, somebody’s chairs set out for the evening. The city has a second ground floor up here that you never see from a taxi.

f12.p: Nothing between you and the plateau is taller than you are. Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure stand in the window base to tip, the kettle is on, and the loudest thing on the terrace is a spoon in a glass.
